arxiv-2007-09114.title: sbi - a toolkit for simulation-based inference
arxiv-2007-09114.creator: Álvaro Tejero-Cantero \;,\; Jan Boelts ,\; Michael Deistler ,\; Jan-Matthis Lueckmann ,\;, Conor Durkan, Pedro J. Gonçalves ,\; David S. Greenberg ,\; Jakob H. Macke, [.3cm] Computational Neuroengineering, TU Munich, School of Informatics, University of Edinburgh, Neural Systems Analysis, Center of
arxiv-2007-09114.description: Abstract Scientists and engineers employ stochastic numerical simulators to model empirically observed phenomena. In contrast to purely statistical models, simulators express scientific principles that provide powerful inductive biases, improve generalization to new data or scenarios and allow for fewer, more interpretable and domain-relevant parameters. Despite these advantages, tuning a simulator’s parameters so that its outputs match data is challenging.

arxiv-2210-02207.title: New results of 0 0 -APN power functions over 𝔽 2 n \mathbb{F}_{2^{n}}
arxiv-2210-02207.creator: Yan-Ping Wang, Zhengbang Zha
arxiv-2210-02207.description: Abstract Partially APN functions attract researchers’ particular interest recently. It plays an important role in studying APN functions. In this paper, based on the multivariate method and resultant elimination, we propose several new infinite classes of 0 0 -APN power functions over 𝔽 2 n \mathbb{F}_{2^{n}} .

arxiv-2308-14475.title: Interactive Multi-Interest Process Pattern Discovery
arxiv-2308-14475.creator: Mozhgan Vazifehdoostirani, Laura Genga, Xixi Lu, Rob Verhoeven, Hanneke van Laarhoven, Remco Dijkman
arxiv-2308-14475.description: Abstract Process pattern discovery methods (PPDMs) aim at identifying patterns of interest to users. Existing PPDMs typically are unsupervised and focus on a single dimension of interest, such as discovering frequent patterns. We present an interactive multi-interest-driven framework for process pattern discovery aimed at identifying patterns that are optimal according to a multi-dimensional analysis goal.

arxiv-2309-05168.title: Multiple Non-radial Solutions for Coupled Schrödinger Equations
arxiv-2309-05168.creator: Xiaopeng Huang, Haoyu Li, Zhi-Qiang Wang
arxiv-2309-05168.description: Abstract The paper deals with the existence of non-radial solutions for an N N -coupled nonlinear elliptic system. In the repulsive regime with some structure conditions on the coupling and for each symmetric subspace of rotation symmetry, we prove the existence of an infinite sequence of non-radial positive solutions and an infinite sequence of non-radial nodal solutions.

arxiv-2310-14559.title: Branch-and-price for prescriptive contagion analytics
arxiv-2310-14559.creator: Alexandre Jacquillat, Michael Lingzhi Li, Martin Ramé, Kai Wang
arxiv-2310-14559.description: Abstract Predictive contagion models are ubiquitous in epidemiology, social sciences, engineering, and management. This paper formulates a prescriptive contagion analytics model where a decision-maker allocates shared resources across multiple segments of a population, each governed by continuous-time dynamics. We define four real-world problems under this umbrella: vaccine distribution, vaccination centers deployment, content promotion, and congestion mitigation.

arxiv-2405-17836.title: An Innovative Networks in Federated Learning
arxiv-2405-17836.creator: Zavareh Bozorgasl, Hao Chen
arxiv-2405-17836.description: Abstract This paper presents the development and application of Wavelet Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (Wav-KAN) in federated learning. We implemented Wav-KAN [ 1 ] in the clients. Indeed, we have considered both continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and also discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to enable multiresolution capabaility which helps in heteregeneous data distribution across clients.

arxiv-2409-01703.title: Piecewise regular solutions to scalar balance laws with singular nonlocal sources
arxiv-2409-01703.creator: Lorena Bociu, Evangelia Ftaka, Khai T. Nguyen, Jacopo Schino
arxiv-2409-01703.description: Abstract The present paper establishes a local well-posed result for piecewise regular solutions with single shock of scalar balance laws with singular integral of convolution type kernels. In a neighborhood of the shock curve, a detailed description of the solution is provided for a general class of initial data. Keyword.

arxiv-2410-03606.title: Programmable time-frequency mode-sorting of single photons with a multi-output quantum pulse gate
arxiv-2410-03606.creator: L. Serino 1,2,*, C. Eigner 2, B. Brecht 1,2, C. Silberhorn 1,2
arxiv-2410-03606.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by L. Serino 1,2,*, C. Eigner 2, B. Brecht 1,2, C. Silberhorn 1,2. We demonstrate a high-dimensional mode-sorter for single photons based on a multi-output quantum pulse gate, which we can program to switch between different temporal-mode encodings including pulse modes, frequency bins, time bins, and their superpositions. This device can facilitate practical realizations of quantum information applications such as high-dimensional quantum key distribution, and thus enables secure communication with enhanced information capacity.

arxiv-2504-21402.title: A product of strongly quasi-nonexpansive mappings in Hadamard spaces
arxiv-2504-21402.creator: Wiparat Worapitpong 1, Parin Chaipunya 2, Poom Kumam 3, Sakan Termkaew 4
arxiv-2504-21402.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove that the product of strongly quasi-nonexpansive Δ \Delta -demiclosed mappings is also a strongly quasi-nonexpansive orbital Δ \Delta -demiclosed mapping in Hadamard spaces. Additionally, we establish the Δ \Delta -convergence theorem for approximating a common fixed point of infinite products of these mappings in Hadamard spaces.

arxiv-2510-06572.title: Boundary Conditions of Warped AdS 3 in New Massive Gravity
arxiv-2510-06572.creator: S. N. Sajadi, Supakchai Ponglertsakul
arxiv-2510-06572.description: Abstract To satisfy the Cardy formula for Warped AdS 3 (WAdS 3 ) solutions in a quadratic ensemble, a specific set of boundary conditions has been proposed in [ 1 ] . In this paper, these boundary conditions have been investigated in the three-dimensional new massive gravity (NMG) framework.

arxiv-2601-07549.title: Exciton coherence propagation measured with non-local four-wave mixing micro-spectroscopy Journal: opticajournal
arxiv-2601-07549.creator: M. Raczyński, A. Dydniański, K. E. Połczyńska, G. Szwed, A. Szczerba, J.-W. Jung, G. Nogues, W. Langbein, P. Kossacki, W. Pacuski, J. Kasprzak
arxiv-2601-07549.description: Abstract Coherence transfer is a multi-disciplinary topic of interest, including chemistry, biology and physics. In quantum technologies, achieving non-local coherent coupling between solid-state qubits is of the utmost importance. Here, we demonstrate that excitons — i.e. electron-hole pairs bound by the Coulomb force within a quantum well — can act as a medium for mesoscopic optical coherence transfer in semiconductors.

arxiv-2601-16402.title: Diffusive and hydrodynamic magnetotransport around a density perturbation in a two-dimensional electron gas
arxiv-2601-16402.creator: P. Shubham Parashar, Michael M. Fogler
arxiv-2601-16402.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by P. Shubham Parashar, Michael M. Fogler. We study current flow around a density inhomogeneity in a two-dimensional electron gas in the presence of a strong magnetic field. The inhomogeneity is parametrized by a power-law tail with an exponent β > 2 \beta>2 . We show that current and electrochemical potential are exponentially suppressed inside a surrounding area much larger than the geometric size of the perturbation. The corresponding “no-go” radius grows as a certain power of the magnetic field.

plos-pone-0012694.description: PLOS ONE research article. Hemozoin (Hz) is a heme crystal that represents a vital pathway for heme disposal in several blood-feeding organisms. Recent evidence demonstrated that β-hematin (βH) (the synthetic counterpart of Hz) formation occurs under physiological conditions near synthetic or biological hy

pmc-11404182.title: Cohort profile: DNA methylation in the Northern Ireland Cohort for the Longitudinal Study of Ageing (NICOLA) – recruitment and participant characteristics
pmc-11404182.creator: Claire Potter, Claire Hill, Laura J Smyth, Charlotte Neville, Angela Scott, Frank Kee, Bernadette McGuinness, Amy McKnight
pmc-11404182.description: AbstractPurposeEpigenetic modifications including DNA methylation (DNAm) are proposed mechanisms by which social or environmental exposures may influence health and behaviours as we age. The Northern Ireland Cohort for the Longitudinal Study of Ageing (NICOLA) DNAm cohort, established in 2013, is one of several worldwide, nationally representative prospective studies of ageing with biological samples from participants who consented to multiomic analysis.

pmc-11480199.title: Overexpression of USP35 enhances the protective effect of hUC-MSCs and their extracellular vesicles in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced SH-SY5Y cells via stabilizing FUNDC1
pmc-11480199.creator: Shuo Wang, Xigong Li, Tianjiao Wang, Zeyu Sun, Erwei Feng, Yongming Jin
pmc-11480199.description: Ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury is associated with neurological disorders such as stroke. The therapeutic potential of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSCs) and their secreted extracellular vesicles (EVs) in alleviating IR injury across various cell types including neuronal cells has been documented.

pmc-11499773.title: AKAP12 positive fibroblast determines immunosuppressive contexture and immunotherapy response in patients with TNBC by promoting macrophage M2 polarization
pmc-11499773.creator: Zhenkun Liu, Siyuan Hu, Xinlei Zhao, Wenxin Xu, Feng Ju, Meiying Gu, Jialei Weng, Yabing Du
pmc-11499773.description: BackgroundTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a molecular subtype of breast cancer with high aggressiveness and poor prognosis. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are major components of the TNBC microenvironment and play an important role in tumor progression and treatment responses. Our goal is to identify specific CAFs subpopulations contributing to TNBC development.

pmc-12409960.title: An Elderly Man with a Solitary Hypopigmented Annular Plaque on the Chest: A Quiz
pmc-12409960.creator: Junzhu XU, Wenting HU
pmc-12409960.description: o fungal elements. Histopathology demonstrated atypical lymphocytes confined to the epidermis and reactive lymphohistiocytic cells in the dermis (Fig 1B). pmc-12496256.title: Robotic ureteral reconstruction for endometriosis-induced strictures: insights from a multi-institutional experience
pmc-12496256.creator: Matthew Lee, Sonam Saxena, Kelley Zhao, Cameron Dodd, Randall Lee, Michael Stifelman, Lee Zhao, Daniel D Eun
pmc-12496256.description: PurposeTo investigate outcomes of robotic ureteral reconstruction (RUR) in female patients with ureteral strictures caused by peri-ureteral endometriosis lesions.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed our multi-institutional Collaborative of Reconstructive Robotic Ureteral Surgery (CORRUS) database to identify all consecutive patients undergoing RUR for surgical management of endometriosis-induced ureteral strictures between 2017 and 2022.

pmc-12533009.title: The relationship between spiritual care needs and religious tendencies of cancer patients
pmc-12533009.creator: Hatice Öntürk Akyüz, Hakime Aslan
pmc-12533009.description: This study was conducted to examine the relationship between the spiritual care needs and religious tendencies of cancer patients. The sample of the study consists of 245 patients treated in the oncology department of a state hospital in eastern Türkiye. Data were collected via face‒to-face meetings technique with inpatients between April and September 2024.

pmc-12751577.title: FGFR1 and FGFR4 are essential regulators of muscle stem cell quiescence
pmc-12751577.creator: Chung-Ju Yeh, Kiran Nakka, Zipora Yablonka-Reuveni, Christoph Lepper
pmc-12751577.description: Quiescence – the reversible growth-arrested G0 state – is critical for the long-term maintenance of many adult stem cells and hence the tissues’ life-long regenerative capacity. Failure to maintain stem cell quiescence during aging leads to stem cell loss and reduced ability to regenerate after injury.

pmc-12787220.title: Real-World Safety of Cyproheptadine-Based Appetite Stimulants: An Electronic Health Record-Based Retrospective Cohort Study in Adult Patients
pmc-12787220.creator: Minoh Ko, Kwangsoo Kim, Heeman Jang, Soomin Lee, Bumkyu Shin, Belong Cho, Seungyeon Kim, Ha Young Jang
pmc-12787220.description: Background: Cyproheptadine-based appetite stimulants (CAS) have been safely used in Korea for over 30 years. However, in older adults who are vulnerable to malnutrition, sarcopenia, and fall-related morbidity, safety of CAS in nutrition care remains uncertain due to limited evidence and its antihistaminic effects.

pmc-13150898.title: Protocol for EACH-ADHF trial: efficacy and safety of early comprehensive rehabilitation in patients with acute decompensated heart failure – a multicentre, randomised controlled trial
pmc-13150898.creator: Mingyu Xu, Jinna Chang, Lan Guo, Bingqing Bai, Rou Wang, Xiangyang Liu, Qian Du, Ying Mao, Ailing Xue, Minting Su, Yanping Wang, Kaixuan Lin, Huan Ma
pmc-13150898.description: IntroductionAcute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is associated with high mortality rates and significant decline in physical function following hospitalisation. Although exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation is recognised as a key component of comprehensive heart failure management, clinical evidence supporting its application in patients with ADHF remains limited.

pmc-13212875.title: The miR396f-GRF7 Module Confers Thermotolerance in Rice
pmc-13212875.creator: Jinsheng Yu, Xinyu Jiang, Xinxin Huang, Yujun Xie, Qiuping Shen, Shen Ni, Nai wu, Bai Li, Qiuhong Luo
pmc-13212875.description: Heat stress is one of the major threats to global rice production globally. Uncovering key genetic regulators of thermotolerance is crucial for breeding climate-resilient crops. While microRNA396 (miR396) is known to be heat-responsive, the function and mechanism of its specific member, miR396f, remain elusive. Here, we report that miR396f is a heat-induced miRNA exhibiting predominantly in vascular bundles.

pmc-13295229.title: Health-related outcomes among adults with cerebral palsy: a scoping review
pmc-13295229.creator: Yeo Wool Kim, Ha Na Jeong, Gi Won Choi, Sun Ju Chang
pmc-13295229.description: BackgroundAdvances in medical technology have extended the life expectancy of individuals with cerebral palsy (CP), resulting in a growing adult population facing long-term physical, psychological, and social health-related challenges. This underscores the need for a comprehensive understanding of their health-related outcomes.

pmc-13442007.title: Disparate privacy risks from medical AI
pmc-13442007.creator: Moritz A Knolle, Martin J Menten, Friederike Jungmann, Felix Meissen, Ben Glocker, Daniel Rueckert, Georgios Kaissis

pmc-13451054.title: Antibiotic leftovers in primary health care: an approach to economic impact and pharmaceutical care *
pmc-13451054.creator: Mariana Lino de Oliveira Santos, Maria Clara Padoveze, Mariana Lino de Oliveira Santos, Maria Clara Padoveze, Mariana Lino de Oliveira Santos, Maria Clara Padoveze
pmc-13451054.description: Objective:To evaluate the results of antibiotic dispensing in a Primary Health Care Unit in the municipality of São Paulo and to explore users’ knowledge regarding the use and disposal of antibiotics through pharmaceutical consultation.Method:A prospective, quantitative study was conducted between January and April 2024, through the analysis of oral antibiotic prescriptions and pharmaceutical consultations using a semi-structured questionnaire.

pmc-13500200.title: Genotype‐Dependent Phenylpropanoid Pathway Specialization in Prunus avium Fruits and Leaves Revealed by Untargeted Metabolomics
pmc-13500200.creator: Giuseppe Ardagna, Sofia Gambini, Alessandra Bulgarini, Stefano Negri, Martino Bianconi, Flavia Di Carlo, Stefania Ceoldo, Flavia Guzzo, Mauro Commisso
pmc-13500200.description: Phenylpropanoids are specialized metabolites involved in multiple aspects of plant physiology and contribute to fruit quality and human health benefits. In sweet cherry ( Prunus avium L.), metabolomic studies have largely focused on fruits, showing that cultivar identity contributes to phenylpropanoid pathway specialization. However, the contribution of genotype to phenylpropanoid organization in other organs, particularly leaves, remains poorly understood.

pmc-13583313.title: Scoring architecture and transparency in healthcare accreditation: A scoping review of measurement design and signalling effects
pmc-13583313.creator: Arjavi Patel, Bhavinkumar Parmar, Sankalp Sagar
pmc-13583313.description: BackgroundHealthcare accreditation is widely adopted to improve quality and strengthen institutional credibility. Although research has examined its associations with organisational processes and clinical outcomes, the internal structure of accreditation decisions remains poorly understood. Specifically, the scoring, weighting, and aggregation processes that transform standards compliance into certification results have received limited analytical attention.

pmc-13714162.title: Expression of the immune checkpoint CD137/CD137L in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and association with histopathological parameters
pmc-13714162.creator: Jacek Glajzer, Jutta Ries, Leah Trumet, Christian Matek, Marco Kesting, Manuel Weber
pmc-13714162.description: As immunotherapy (IT) with checkpoint inhibitors continues to make rapid progress in the treatment of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), response rates still necessitate substantial improvement. Current concepts to improve therapy response mainly consider identification of further immunological targets eligible for extension of IT.
